extracted.intended_audience: SIGCHI community: HCI researchers, practitioners, conference attendees, reviewers, and authors
extracted.subtask_description: Announcing and describing the CHI Steering Committee working group's multi-year effort to redesign peer review for CHI full papers, and soliciting community feedback on the proposed changes. The page summarizes methods used (community input, benchmarking, data simulations, role‑playing) and points readers to a 5‑point action plan and feedback channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community input and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2024, a working group ... has been working on reimagining peer review. We have held community input sessions, had an online feedback forum, and have met regularly over the last 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The working group solicits and incorporates community feedback; readers may provide feedback in person at CHI 2026 (Wednesday afternoon at 2:15 in the Auditorium) or via an online form. The process is explicitly participatory and seeks broad community engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking other conferences and review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: We created reports on what other conferences (within SIGCHI and the ACM, but also beyond) have been doing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The working group looked beyond CHI to understand alternative models and drew inspiration from other review processes (e.g., grants, faculty searches, graduate application reviews, university rankings) when evaluating options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of previous CHI submission data to run simulations
rubrics_metrics.description: We used previous CHI submission data to run simulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about review-structure changes are informed by empirical analysis and simulation of historical submission data to predict impacts of proposed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role‑playing exercises of different review structures
rubrics_metrics.description: We engaged in role‑playing exercises where we enacted different review structures and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical enactment and scenario testing (role‑play) were used as a method to surface strengths and weaknesses of candidate review processes before selecting a proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative stakeholder consultation and governance review
rubrics_metrics.description: We sought input and feedback from various stakeholders and discussed it with the CHI Steering Committee and the SIGCHI Executive Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process included iterative consultation with governance bodies and stakeholders, indicating that proposed changes are reviewed at multiple organizational levels before adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce an actionable, interconnected proposal (5‑point action plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: This all culminated in an in‑person meeting in January 2026, where we finalized our proposal for CHI full papers review processes moving forward. Our proposal is a 5‑point action plan, with interconnected solutions which can be found at this link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The outcome is intended to be concrete and actionable (a 5‑point plan). The page points readers to the proposal for full details and frames the plan as interconnected solutions rather than isolated changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent reporting/documentation of process
rubrics_metrics.description: We created reports on what other conferences ... have been doing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation and reporting of the investigation (reports, summaries) are used to justify and explain the rationale for proposed changes, supporting transparency in how conclusions were reached.
